authorities.name: Environmental Protection Act 1990, s.82(1)-(2)
authorities.date_note: Enactment year. The text verified this session is the current in-force version; the page notes multiple amendments extending through 2026, with some outstanding modifications not yet in force.
authorities.proposition: A magistrates' court may act on a complaint of statutory nuisance made by any person on the ground that they are aggrieved by the existence of that nuisance (s.82(1)) - the standing threshold construed in Watkins below. Once satisfied a nuisance exists, or is likely to recur, the court must make an abatement or prohibition order (s.82(2)).
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly this session, independently re-fetched and re-confirmed a second time - both fetches consistent on s.82(1)'s exact text.

authorities.name: Watkins v Aged Merchant Seamen's Homes
authorities.court: High Court (Queen's Bench Division, Administrative Court)
authorities.proposition: A person does not need a legally enforceable right of occupation to be a 'person aggrieved' for standing under s.82(1) - ordinarily, a person in actual occupation when the complaint is made is aggrieved simply because they are occupying the premises and at risk of prejudice to their health if the premises are in a state constituting a statutory nuisance, even where their right to remain is legally contested or has since been terminated. This is subject to a narrow exception where the complainant is acting as a 'mere busybody' in bad faith. Standing is assessed as at the date the complaint is made, not by reference to later events.
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly from Find Case Law this session, independently re-fetched and re-confirmed a second time - both fetches consistent on paragraph 41's actual-occupation holding. BAILII returned HTTP 403 and was not used - not needed here since Find Case Law covers this post-2009 case directly.

edges.verified_via: Watkins v Aged Merchant Seamen's Homes [2018] EWHC 2410 (Admin), paras 36 and 41, fetched directly from Find Case Law and independently re-confirmed: construes 'aggrieved' in s.82(1) as ordinarily satisfied by actual occupation alone.

what_this_is_not: Two verified nodes covering standing to bring a statutory nuisance complaint. Does not cover the definition of 'statutory nuisance' itself in detail (s.79), contaminated land liability (Part IIA), biodiversity net gain duties under the Environment Act 2021, or any other Environmental Law subject - all remain unbuilt.
